chunks: When the soul is taken, it hovers above the body—the soul of the believer and of other than him—looking at everything that is done with it. Then, when he is shrouded and placed upon the bier and carried on the shoulders of men, the soul returns to him and enters into him. Then his sight is extended for him, and he looks at his place in Paradise or from the Fire. So he calls out at the top of his voice: if he is among the people of Paradise, 'Hasten me, hasten me!' and if he is among the people of the Fire, 'Take me back, take me back!' And he knows everything that is done with him and hears the speech.

key_terms.الرُّوحُ: the soul that is taken at death and remains perceptive
key_terms.السَّرِيرِ: the bier on which the deceased is placed
key_terms.النَّارِ: the Fire, the abode shown to the condemned deceased
key_terms.الْجَسَدِ: the body over which the soul hovers after being taken
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, the abode shown to the blessed deceased
key_terms.بِأَعْلَى صَوْتِهِ: with his loudest voice, indicating the force of his call

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say happens to the soul after death and during burial?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the state of the soul immediately after death and during the funeral procession. It indicates that the deceased perceives what is being done to the body and is shown a place in Paradise or the Fire, reflecting the reality of the afterlife and barzakh.
